subject: math
domain: Conditional Probability and the Rules of Probability
cluster: Understand independence and conditional probability and use them to interpret data

items.prompt:
A two-way table organizes data by:
A) One category
B) Two categories
C) No categories
D) Three categories

steps: Rows and columns are two categories.

items.prompt:
Of $100$ people, $40$ like coffee. $P(\text{coffee})$ is:
A) $0.04$
B) $0.4$
C) $4$
D) $40$

A conditional probability 'given tea' uses:
A) The whole table
B) The tea row only
C) The grand total
D) The coffee column only

Of $50$ tea-drinkers, $20$ like coffee. $P(\text{coffee}\mid\text{tea})$ is:
A) $0.2$
B) $0.4$
C) $0.5$
D) $0.7$

Of $80$ students, $48$ passed. $P(\text{pass})$ is:
A) $0.48$
B) $0.6$
C) $0.8$
D) $0.32$

To check independence from a table, see if:
A) $P(A\mid B)=P(A)$
B) $P(A)=1$
C) $P(B)=0$
D) Counts are equal

steps: Independence means the conditional equals the overall probability.

items.prompt:
$P(\text{dog})=0.5$ but $P(\text{dog}\mid\text{cat})=0.4$. Owning a dog and a cat are:
A) Independent
B) Dependent
C) Impossible
D) Equal

Of $40$ girls, $24$ play a sport, and overall $P(\text{sport})=0.6$. Sport and gender are:
A) Dependent
B) Independent
C) Impossible
D) Complementary
